title: Mosaic batcher tuning: entropy-aware scheduling and KV-resident trimming for mixed prompt/response workloads
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Background: Our continuous batcher experiences degraded tail latency and uneven GPU memory pressure when workloads contain a high variance of prompt/response lengths (e.g., short prompts with long generated responses and vice versa). The existing length-priority bins reduce some tail impact but leave KV cache fragmentation and GPU slab fragmentation that increases p95/p99 latency and token cost during realistic customer traffic patterns.

Goal: Implement and tune a new scheduler variant (Mosaic batcher) that blends entropy-aware length clustering, adaptive admission control, and proactive KV-residence trimming to reduce tail latency, decrease KV churn, and improve effective GPU memory utilization for mixed-length workloads without sacrificing average throughput.

Scope: Prototype and evaluate in staging, add observability + rollout plan, canary to 5% of traffic, and full rollout contingent on meeting acceptance criteria. This ticket covers design, initial implementation in the scheduler layer, integration with KV-residency manager, benchmark runs, and rollout playbook. Follow-ups (metrics dashboards, long-term heuristics) will be separate tickets.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency <= baseline p95 * 1.05 for 99th percentile length-mixed traces (no regression)
p99 latency reduction >= 10% on our mixed-length benchmark (compared to current continuous batcher) or equivalent improvement in token efficiency
GPU memory fragmentation metric (slab fragmentation index) reduces by >= 12% on representative workloads
KV cache churn (evictions/sec) reduces by >= 15% under sustained mixed-turn traffic
No production errors introduced in canary (error rate remains within historical variance)
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rolloutable via console canary controls
comments: 2026-03-03 - Liam Chen: Spike results attached in design doc. Early experiments show 8% p99 reduction on synthetic skewed-turn workload using length-cluster admission and gentle KV trimming based on token-density heuristic.

2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Plan to prototype scheduler hook and separate KV-residence controller so we can A/B the admission strategy independently of eviction policy. Will add flags for 'entropy_threshold' and 'kv_trim_lookahead'.

2026-03-08 - PM review (Sofia Martinez): Please include customer-facing risk section in the playbook for Canary; call out potential short-term throughput drop vs long-term token cost improvement. Prioritize observable rollout metrics.

2026-03-09 - Eng review (Ravi Narayanan): Implementation note: avoid global locks when computing cluster assignments; use per-worker histograms and a background coalescer to recompute cluster boundaries every 250ms. Also add defensive fallback to current binning when memory pressure > 92%.

2026-03-11 - Aisha Patel: Benchmark run #4 (8xA100 staging) attached. Mosaic reduced p99 by 13% and KV evictions by 18% on mixed conversation trace (50% short prompts, 50% long responses). Observed a 3% drop in average throughput during cold cache; mitigation: slower admission ramp and prefetch for anticipated long continuations.

2026-03-12 - Liam Chen: Created PR for scheduler core and KV-trim controller. Requests: performance review, unit tests for cluster boundary updates, and integration test that simulates interleaved short/long turn arrivals.
implementation_notes:
Core changes: introduce MosaicCoordinator in scheduler layer responsible for
1) entropy estimation across incoming sequence-length histogram
2) dynamic cluster boundary computation (fast-path for low variance, multi-cluster for high variance)
3) admission policy that biases slot allocation to minimize slot stretch for long-turns

KV-residence controller: conservative trimming policy that marks low-density prefixes for compaction (based on recent access frequency and continuation probability). Trimming is asynchronous and uses slab-aware free lists to reduce fragmentation.
GPU memory: add slab-defrag hint writes and align small allocations to 256B buckets where possible; expose slab fragmentation metric to Grafana and use it for conservative fallback thresholding.
Rollout flags: mosaic_enabled, mosaic_entropy_threshold, kv_trim_lookahead_ms, mosaic_admission_scalar. All defaulted to off/very conservative in runtime config.
Bench harness: reuse existing mixed-length trace suite but add an 'asymmetric-turn' scenario that alternates 1-token prompts with 1024-token generation to stress KV and slab allocation patterns.
